US-119-HR10371.title: Ensuring SBA Implementation of GAO Recommendations Act of 2026
US-119-HR10371.summary:
Ensuring SBA Implementation of GAO Recommendations Act of 2026

This bill requires the Office of Veterans Business Development within the Small Business Administration (SBA) to develop and implement policies and procedures to ensure compliance with existing reporting requirements related to veteran-owned small businesses. Specifically, such policies must ensure the SBA complies and submits an annual report on the needs of small businesses owned and controlled by veterans, including service-disabled veterans. Such reports must also include proposals to improve the access of such businesses to government assistance.

US-119-HR10371.aiSummary: The bill would direct a Small Business Administration office to set up policies and steps to meet current reporting rules for veteran-owned small businesses. US-119-HR10591.title: Safer Choice Program Authorization Act of 2026

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10591.description: To authorize the Safer Choice Program within the Environmental Protection Agency, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10591.aiSummary: The bill would set up and authorize the EPA’s Safer Choice Program, a voluntary program that identifies products made with safer chemical ingredients. It would let the EPA certify products, allow use of the Safer Choice and Design for the Environment labels, and set rules for review, public reports, and a public product database. It would affect manufacturers, retailers, and other groups that want to take part in the program.

US-119-HR9382.title: To require the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to link together applications of family members throughout the NEXUS application process, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR9382.summary:
This bill requires U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to link the applications of family members (parents, legal guardians, children, grandparents, grandchildren, and siblings residing within a single household) throughout the NEXUS application process (an expedited border inspections program between the United-States and Canada).

CBP must permit a family member to schedule NEXUS interviews for all linked family members and may provide linked family members the option to participate in joint interviews.

CBP may exempt from the interview process a child under 14 years of age who is linked to an eligible family member.

US-119-HR10173.description: To amend the America COMPETES Reauthorization Act of 2010 to reauthorize the research experiences for undergraduates program at the National Science Foundation, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10173.aiSummary: The bill would reauthorize the National Science Foundation’s Research Experiences for Undergraduates program, which gives undergrads research jobs and training in science and engineering. It would expand rules for who can take part, with extra focus on students from schools with fewer research chances, first-generation college students, and other underrepresented groups. It would authorize $100 million each year from fiscal years 2027 through 2032 for the program.

US-119-HR10052.title: Right to Worship Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10052.policyArea: Civil Rights and Liberties, Minority Issues
US-119-HR10052.description: To protect the right to the free exercise of religion.
US-119-HR10052.aiSummary: The bill would make it unlawful to knowingly disrupt or block people from taking part in a scheduled religious service near a house of worship, within 100 feet of an entry during the hour before and after the service. It would affect people near places of worship and could lead to civil fines and lawsuits. The bill also lets the U.S. Attorney General or a state attorney general bring a civil case.

US-119-S254.title: ARTIST Act
US-119-S254.summary:
Alaska’s Right to Ivory Sales and Tradition Act or the ARTIST Act

This act prohibits states from imposing bans on marine mammal products produced by Alaska Natives.

Specifically, states may not prohibit the interstate commerce, importation, sale, transfer, trade, barter, or possession of marine mammal ivory, marine mammal bone, or baleen legally produced by an Alaska Native as an authentic Alaska Native article of handicrafts and clothing.

US-119-S331.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
US-119-S331.summary:
Halt All Lethal Trafficking of Fentanyl Act or the HALT Fentanyl Act

This act permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class into schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act. A schedule I controlled substance is a drug, substance, or chemical that has a high potential for abuse; has no currently accepted medical value; and is subject to regulatory controls and administrative, civil, and criminal penalties under the Controlled Substances Act.

Under the act, offenses involving fentanyl-related substances are triggered by the same quantity thresholds and subject to the same penalties as offenses involving fentanyl analogues (e.g., offenses involving 100 grams or more trigger a 10-year mandatory minimum prison term).

Additionally, the act establishes a new, alternative registration process for certain schedule I research.

The act also makes several other changes to registration requirements for conducting research with controlled substances, including
• permitting a single registration for related research sites in certain circumstances,
• waiving the requirement for a new inspection in certain situations, and
• allowing a registered researcher to perform certain manufacturing activities with small quantities of a substance without obtaining a manufacturing registration.

Finally, the act expresses the sense that Congress agrees with the interpretation of the Controlled Substances Act in United States v. McCray , a 2018 case decided by the U.S. District Court for the Western District of New York. In that case, the court held that butyryl fentanyl, a controlled substance, can be considered an analogue of fentanyl even though, under the Controlled Substances Act, the term controlled substance analogue specifically excludes a controlled substance.

US-119-S331.aiSummary: The law permanently puts fentanyl-related substances into the most restricted drug category under federal law. It sets the same quantity triggers and penalties for those substances as for fentanyl analogues, including a 10-year minimum prison term for offenses involving 100 grams or more. It also creates a new way to register some schedule I research and changes some research rules, including single-site registration in some cases, skipping a new inspection in some cases, and limited small-scale manufacturing by registered researchers.
